Moral Foundations Theory is a framework that separates human morality into the following categories:

  - Care/Harm: related to our long evolution as mammals with attachment systems
    and an ability to feel (and dislike) the pain of others. It underlies the
    virtues of kindness, gentleness, and nurturance.

  - Loyalty/Betrayal: related to our long history as tribal creatures able to
    form shifting coalitions. It is active anytime people feel that it is "one
    for all and all for one." It underlies the virtues of patriotism and
    self-sacrifice for the group.

  - Authority/Subversion: shaped by our long primate history of hierarchical
    social interactions. It underlies virtues of leadership and followership,
    including deference to prestigious authority figures and respect for
    traditions.

  - Sanctity/Purity: shaped by the psychology of disgust and contamination. It
    underlies notions of striving to live in an elevated, less carnal, more
    noble, and more "natural" way (often present in religious narratives). This
    foundation underlies the widespread idea that the body is a temple that can
    be desecrated by immoral activities and contaminants (an idea not unique to
    religious traditions). It underlies the virtues of self-discipline,
    self-improvement, naturalness, and spirituality.

  - Equality: related to our intuitions about equal treatment and equal outcome
    for individuals.

  - Proportionality: related to our intuitions about individuals getting
    rewarded in proportion to their merit or contribution.

Every category has a bidirectional nature. For example:

One person's sensitivity to the Care/Harm foundation may lead them to support high levels of immigration from poorer nations, to reduce the suffering of those who migrate. Whereas another person's sensitivity to the very same foundation may lead them to oppose those levels, because they believe it could lead to people they care about being harmed.

# Labour Party Manifesto 2024 Summary

## Core Economic Policy
Labour proposes fiscal rules requiring the current budget to balance and debt to fall as a share of GDP by the fifth forecast year. They commit to capping corporation tax at 25%, maintaining the triple lock on state pensions, and not increasing income tax, National Insurance, or VAT. They plan to abolish non-dom status, close private equity tax loopholes, and strengthen HMRC to tackle tax avoidance.

## Economic Growth Strategy
A National Wealth Fund (£7.3 billion) will invest in ports, gigafactories, steel, carbon capture, and green hydrogen. A new Industrial Strategy Council will guide long-term economic planning. Planning reform aims to build 1.5 million homes, with brownfield sites prioritised and strategic greenbelt release. Business rates will be reformed to support high streets against online retailers.

## Energy and Environment
Great British Energy, a publicly-owned company headquartered in Scotland (£8.3 billion capitalisation), will partner with industry on clean power. Targets include doubling onshore wind, tripling solar, and quadrupling offshore wind by 2030. The windfall tax on oil and gas companies will be extended and increased. No new oil/gas exploration licences will be issued, though existing fields continue operating. The Warm Homes Plan allocates £6.6 billion for home energy upgrades.

## NHS and Social Care
Plans include 40,000 additional weekly appointments, doubling CT/MRI scanners, recruiting 8,500 mental health staff, and delivering the NHS workforce plan. Dentistry measures include 700,000 urgent appointments. Social care reform aims toward a National Care Service with national standards. Mental health legislation will be modernised.

## Education
Recruitment of 6,500 teachers funded by ending VAT exemption for private schools. Free breakfast clubs in all primary schools. 3,000 new primary school nurseries. Curriculum and assessment review planned. Skills England will coordinate training, with the Apprenticeships Levy reformed into a Growth and Skills Levy.

## Crime and Justice
A Neighbourhood Policing Guarantee will recruit thousands of officers. Knife crime reduction targets halving within a decade, with new Young Futures hubs. Violence against women measures include specialist rape units in every police force and fast-tracked rape cases. Prisons will be expanded using planning powers.

## Immigration and Borders
A Border Security Command with counter-terrorism powers will target smuggling gangs. The Rwanda scheme will be scrapped. A returns unit with 1,000 additional staff will fast-track removals. Work visa policy will link to skills training requirements.

## Workers' Rights
Legislation within 100 days will ban exploitative zero-hours contracts, end fire-and-rehire practices, and establish day-one employment rights. A Single Enforcement Body will oversee compliance. The minimum wage will account for cost of living, with age bands removed.

## Constitutional Reform
Hereditary peers will lose voting rights. A mandatory retirement age of 80 will apply to Lords members. An Ethics and Integrity Commission will be established. Voting age will be lowered to 16.

## Devolution
A Council of Nations and Regions will bring together UK and devolved leaders. Structural fund allocation returns to devolved governments. Adult skills funding will be devolved to Combined Authorities.

## Foreign Policy
NATO commitment remains absolute, with a Strategic Defence Review within the first year. Support for Ukraine continues. An improved EU relationship is sought without rejoining the single market or customs union, including veterinary agreements and security cooperation. Palestinian statehood recognition is supported.

# Reform UK Manifesto 2024 Summary

## Overview
Reform UK presents a policy document outlining proposed changes across multiple sectors, with claimed potential savings of £150 billion annually and costs of £141 billion annually, plus projected growth-related tax revenues of £10 billion.

## Immigration
The party proposes freezing non-essential immigration, leaving the European Convention on Human Rights, and establishing offshore processing for asylum seekers. Foreign workers would face a 20% National Insurance rate (up from 13.8%), with exemptions for healthcare workers and small businesses. A five-year residency requirement would apply before accessing benefits. Student dependents would be barred, and foreign criminals would face immediate deportation.

## Economic Proposals
**Personal taxation:** Raise the income tax threshold to £20,000, keeping the basic rate at 20% with higher rate starting at £70,000. Stamp duty would be eliminated below £750,000. Inheritance tax would be abolished for estates under £2 million.

**Business:** Corporation tax threshold raised to £100,000 profits, with the main rate reduced from 25% to 15% over time. VAT threshold increased to £150,000. Business rates abolished for high street SMEs, offset by a 4% online delivery tax on large multinationals.

## Public Spending
Proposed 5% efficiency savings across departments (£50 billion). The Bank of England would stop paying interest on QE reserves (£35 billion). Foreign aid cut by 50% (£6 billion savings).

## NHS
Zero basic rate tax for frontline NHS staff for three years. 20% tax relief on private healthcare. Patient voucher scheme for treatment if waiting times exceed specified limits (3 days for GPs, 3 weeks for consultants, 9 weeks for operations).

## Energy
Scrap Net Zero commitments and renewable energy subsidies. Fast-track North Sea oil and gas licensing. Pursue shale gas exploration and small modular nuclear reactors.

## Policing and Justice
Recruit 40,000 new police officers over five years. Build 10,000 new detention places. Mandatory life sentences for violent repeat offenders. Reopen local magistrates' courts.

## Education
20% tax relief on independent school fees. Student loan interest scrapped. Restrict undergraduate numbers and enforce minimum entry standards.

## Defence
Increase defence spending to 3% of GDP within six years. Pay increases for armed forces personnel. Create dedicated Veterans ministry.

## Housing and Planning
Fast-track brownfield development. Abolish the Renters Reform Bill. Remove Section 24 restrictions for landlords. Prioritise local residents for social housing.

## Constitutional Changes
Leave ECHR and reform Human Rights Act. Reform House of Lords. Restrict postal voting. Hold referendum on proportional representation.

## Other Policies
- Increase farming budget to £3 billion
- End automatic EU fishing access to UK waters
- Royal Commission on social care
- Scrap HS2, ban ULEZ zones
- Reform BBC funding model
